We love learning, building, and solving real-world problems through technology. We are looking for motivated, curious, and collaborative people with skills in programming, data science, AI/ML, data visualization, GIS, UI/UX, or scientific research. 🚀
summary: MODIS and VIIRS observe active fires at different spatial resolutions and with different detection opportunities, so their hotspot counts cannot be joined directly. Fyrora matches contemporaneous Aqua MODIS and S-NPP VIIRS passes on a shared 10 km equal-area grid, learns a guarded MODIS-equivalent count mapping, and presents the result as a coverage-aware historical activity calendar. Users can compare region, year, and day/night views, run a bounded Western Iberia area-of-interest analysis, and download daily results. Unsupported matched-detection days remain unknown rather than being converted to zero. The prototype is intended for transparent historical analysis and planning, not emergency warning.
details:
PROBLEM

A satellite transition can resemble a change in fire activity even when the difference comes from sensor resolution, sensitivity, or observation opportunity. Directly concatenating MODIS and VIIRS detections can therefore create false historical trends.

SOLUTION AND METHOD

Fyrora pairs contemporaneous Aqua MODIS and S-NPP VIIRS detection-derived passes by region, UTC date, day/night and a maximum 60-minute separation. Both sensors are aggregated to a shared 10 km Lambert equal-area grid. A Poisson-loss histogram gradient-boosting model maps VIIRS context to MODIS-equivalent hotspot counts using a 3×3 neighborhood, scan footprint, season, latitude, day/night and pass-time difference. The protocol fits 2017–2018, selects on 2019 and evaluates 2020 outside those steps. We also use date-block bootstrap, four leave-one-region-out tests and locked later-year transfer tests. Unsupported matched-detection days remain null rather than zero.

WEB APPLICATION

Users can explore region, year and day/night views; inspect historical-percentile calendars; export CSV; run a validated Western Iberia bounding-box and date-range workflow; and inspect an Evidence Passport that links claims to versioned artifacts and hashes. A separate Victoria 2024 explorer shows descriptive MODIS, S-NPP VIIRS and NOAA-20 VIIRS FIRMS records on an OpenStreetMap map.

EVIDENCE

The pipeline normalizes 2,587,488 observations from 2017–2020 and matches 5,314 passes. On the temporal 2020 evaluation, count WAPE improves from 1.224 for a fixed-ratio baseline to 0.832 for the selected model, a 32.0% reduction, while Spearman correlation improves from 0.045 to 0.635. All four leave-one-region-out tests improve. A locked 2024 test across three new fire regimes improves pooled WAPE from 1.369 to 1.084, although WAPE remains above 1 in two regions, so we do not claim global or operational accuracy. A 2023 EFFIS outcome gate failed and is openly reported; operationalReady remains false.

TOOLS

Python, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, PyArrow, GeoPandas/Shapely/PyProj, H3, Parquet, CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet, OpenStreetMap, Docker, Nginx, Pytest and SHA-256 provenance manifests.

IMPACT AND LIMITATIONS

Fyrora helps scientists and land managers examine historical burning patterns without mistaking a sensor change for a real trend. It complements, rather than replaces, operational services such as Copernicus EFFIS. It is not a live alert, burned-area estimate or life-safety system. Detection-derived pairs do not establish complete satellite coverage or unique-fire counts; FRP remains experimental.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE DISCLOSURE

SI tools assisted brainstorming, research and documentation support, coding/debugging, data-analysis review, English–Turkish translation, UI/UX iteration and preparation of the slide presentation. Scientific methods, transformations, metrics, claims and limitations were reviewed against committed data artifacts and automated tests. No SI-generated NASA branding, imagery, audio or video is included.
